newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Embattled S.African oil rig set for sea trials.
newsitem.headline: Embattled S.African oil rig set for sea trials.

text.p: The embattled Soekor-Energy Africa oil rig was finally due to leave Simon's Town harbour on Monday for testing and sea trials.
Soekor project manager Andre van Niekerk told Reuters that the Orca would be anchored in the False Bay area for the next three days while tests were undertaken.
"Certification by the American Bureau of Shipping and the Department of Mineral and Energy Affairs will be carried out during this period," Van Niekerk said.
It would then be towed to the Oribi oilfield off Mossel Bay for the commissioning of South Africa's first oilfield by April this year. It had originally been scheduled to start up in February.

The Orca was delayed in Simon's Town last week when it was "arrested" by the sheriff's office because of a 31 million rand debt owed by a French contractor Schlumberger, which is refurbishing the rig, to local sub-contractor Babcock Construction.
This meant the Orca was not able to leave for sea trials as scheduled. Strong winds also made departure impossible.
While lawyers sorted out the legal wrangle, the crew used the time to cary out some of the tests needed to certify the rig.

The Oribi oilfield is expected to initially produce 20,000 barrels of oil a day, with this amount tapering off over three to six years. It will form the nucleus for the subsequent development of several other nearby oil discoveries, which will extend production life by a further six years.

Soekor and its 20 percent partner, Energy Africa Ltd , plan to pump the oil into a one million barrel shuttle tanker for shipment to one of South Africa's three coastal refineries in Cape Town or Durban.
